claim: The receiving party shall not disclose confidential information.
Confidential information includes all written materials marked as confidential.
The receiving party may use confidential information only for the evaluation purpose.
Confidential information does not include information in the public domain.
The obligations of confidentiality shall survive for a period of three years.
The receiving party shall return or destroy confidential information upon request.
Disclosure of confidential information is permitted when required by law.
The receiving party shall limit access to confidential information on a need-to-know basis.
All confidential information shall be stored securely.
The receiving party shall notify the disclosing party of any unauthorized disclosure.
The receiving party shall indemnify the disclosing party for all breaches.
This agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California.
Either party may assign this agreement without the other party's consent.
The prevailing party shall recover all legal fees and costs.
The term of this agreement shall be five years from the effective date.
The receiving party may sublicense confidential information to affiliates.
All confidential information must be marked with the disclosing party's logo.
The receiving party shall pay a royalty of 5 percent on net sales.
Confidential information shall be subject to mandatory audit by the disclosing party.
The receiving party shall appoint a data protection officer.
